title: Isolation of intact and active FoF1 ATP synthase using a FLAG-tagged subunit from the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
protocol: Resuspend collected Synechocystis 6803 cells in buffer A.
Break cells using Precellys 24 homogenizer with 6 cycles of 25 s at 6,000 rpm in the presence of glass beads.
Centrifuge at 4,000 × g for 10 min and remove the pellet fraction.
Centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 1 h and keep the pellet fraction which is the crude membranes.
Re-suspend the collected membrane pellet thoroughly using FLAG buffer, and incubate on ice for 0.5–1 h to solubilize the membranes.
Measure the protein concentration of the membrane solution.
Adjust the protein concentration to 5–10 mg/mL with FLAG buffer.
Slowly add dodecylmaltoside (DDM) to a final concentration of 1% (w/v), and incubate for 1 h with gentle agitation.
Centrifuge the membrane solution at 20,000 × g for 30 min to remove insoluble debris.
Filter the resulting supernatant through 0.45 μm membrane.
Re-suspend the Anti-FLAG M2 affinity resin thoroughly.
Transfer 1 mL of resin into a clean, empty chromatography column for 5 OD of Synechocystis 6803 cells.
Drain the gel bed naturally.
Wash the resin with three sequential column volumes (CV) of 0.1 M glycine-HCl (pH 3.5).
Do not leave the resin in glycine-HCl for longer than 20 minutes.
Wash the resin with five CV of FLAG buffer to equilibrate the resin.
Keep the gel bed wet throughout the process.
Load the membrane lysate onto the prepared column under gravity flow.
Reload the flow through membrane lysate sample twice to increase binding.
Repeat the loading-washing-elution procedure if necessary to accumulate more proteins.
Wash the column with 5–15 times of 2 CV of FLAG buffer supplemented with 0.03% (w/v) DDM.
Elute the FLAG-tagged ATPase with 2 times of 1.5 CV of FLAG buffer supplemented with 150 μg/mL 3×FLAG peptide and 0.03% (w/v) DDM.
Concentrate the eluate using a 100 KDa cutoff ultra-centrifugal filter to remove most of the 3×FLAG peptide and overexpressed ATPase subunit.
Change the buffer after concentrating the eluate.
Perform the elution step at a temperature of about 22°C–25°C, keeping samples on ice.
Check the integrity and purity of isolated ATPase before conducting biochemistry analysis.
Conduct SDS-PAGE analysis of the isolated ATPase.
Perform Western blot analysis of the isolated ATPase.
Optionally, check the isolated ATPase using native PAGE such as blue-native PAGE.
Conduct mass spectrometry to identify protein components in the isolated ATPase.
Mix samples 1:1 with 2× SDS protein solubilization buffer for a final concentration of 5% SDS.
Reduce samples by adding 5 mM TCEP and incubating for 10 min at 95°C.
Alkylate samples by adding iodacetamide to a final concentration of 10 mM and incubating for 20 min at about 22°C–25°C in the dark.
Add 12% aqueous phosphoric acid at 1:10 ratio for a final concentration of ∼1.2% phosphoric acid and mix.
Add at least 6 times the current sample volume of S-Trap protein binding buffer to the sample.
Place the S-Trap micro column in a 2 mL tube to collect flow through.
Pipette the acidified sample onto the S-Trap micro column.
Centrifuge the micro column at 4,000 g until all sample has passed through the S-Trap column.
Add 150 μL of S-Trap protein binding buffer to wash captured proteins.
Repeat washing procedure three times by adding and centrifuging buffer.
Move the S-Trap micro column with trapped sample to a clean 1.5 mL low-bind sample tube for digestion.
Add 20 μL of Digestion buffer containing trypsin at 1:10–1:25 (wt:wt) onto the top of the micro column.
Use at least 0.75 μg of trypsin for effective digestions.
Ensure there is no air bubble between the protease digestion solution and the protein trap.
Incubate the mixture for 1 hour at 47°C.
Add 40 μL of 50 mM Digestion buffer, then centrifuge at 4,000 × g for approximately 1 minute to elute peptides.
Add 40 μL of 0.2% aqueous formic acid, then centrifuge at 4,000 × g for approximately 1 minute to elute peptides a second time.
Add 35 μL of 50% acetonitrile containing 0.2% formic acid, then centrifuge at 4,000 × g for approximately 1 minute to elute peptides the last time.
Dry the peptide solution completely in a SpeedVac.
Resuspend dried peptides in 25 μL H2O and perform a BCA assay to determine the peptide concentration.
Analyze one ug of peptides on a Q-Exactive Plus mass spectrometer coupled with an EASY-nLC 1000 UHPLC system.
Use a self-packed analytical column with silica beads coated with C18 for MS measurement.
Apply a linear gradient ranging from 5% to 40% buffer B over the first 90 minutes and from 40% to 100% buffer B in the subsequent 30 minutes for peptide separation.

Perform survey scans at 70,000 resolution with an AGC target of 3e6 and a maximum injection time of 50 ms followed by fragmentation scans of top 10 precursor ions at 17,500 resolution with 1.6 m/z isolation windows, NCE of 30, and dynamic exclusion time of 35 seconds.
Set the intensity threshold to 1.3e5 for all MS2 scans, AGC to 1e4, and maximum injection time to 80 ms.
Analyze raw data with MaxQuant (v 1.6.14.0) allowing two missed cleavage sites, no variable modifications, and carbamidomethylation of cysteines as fixed modification.
Use unique peptides for quantification using the iBAQ algorithm.
